cards.text: Jesus is in a house with His disciples, still teaching them about the kingdom of heaven (Matt 13:36). Now He says it's like treasure hidden in a field. Friend, if I found treasure in a field, the WHOLE Dorinverse would hear me yelling about it.

cards.question: A man finds that treasure hidden in the field. What's the first thing he does with it?
After he hides the treasure again, the man goes and sells all he has. What does he buy with it?
True or false: the man in the field is gloomy about selling all he has.

cards.text: Again, Jesus says the kingdom of heaven is like a merchant in search of fine pearls. I picture this man squinting at every pearl in town like it's hiding something from him.

cards.question: The merchant finds one very precious pearl. True or false: to buy it, he sells all he has.

cards.text: Once again, Jesus paints a new picture: the kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea. Fields, pearls, now fishing, and Jesus is covering EVERY job in town!

cards.question: In Jesus' picture, a net gets cast into the sea. What does it catch?

cards.text: When the net is full, the men pull it ashore and sit down. I bet that job takes a while, kind of like me going over a fresh batch, cookie by cookie.

cards.question: Sitting on the shore, the men sort the ___ fish into containers and throw the ___ away.

cards.text: Then Jesus says it will be like that at the end of the age. Friend, this is where the fishing story gets serious.

cards.question: Jesus says that at the end of the age, the ___ will come and separate the wicked from the righteous.
At the end of the age, the angels separate the wicked from the righteous. Where does Jesus say they throw the wicked?

cards.text: Jesus says there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth there. Then He asks His disciples, "Have you understood all these things?"

cards.question: True or false: when Jesus asks if they've understood all these things, the disciples answer yes.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them that every scribe who has been discipled in the kingdom of heaven is like a homeowner with a storeroom. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, so I RESPECT a man with storage.

cards.question: Jesus says that homeowner brings out of his storeroom ___ treasures as well as ___.

findings.problem: The joke is about Jesus himself ('Jesus is covering EVERY job in town!'). Its subject is how Jesus teaches, not Papa Dorin or a person in the story. It also doesn't land cleanly: the man who finds the treasure is never called a field worker, so 'every job in town' needs explaining.

rule.text: His humor never targets God, Jesus, Scripture or the Marriage Supper.

findings.problem: The joke 'I bet that job takes a while, kind of like me going over a fresh batch, cookie by cookie' is a pleasant aside, not a real laugh. It needs to be pushed further.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the exact wording 'new treasures as well as old.' Card 16 gives no setup the baker could reason from, such as what a discipled scribe brings out. It tests wording the baker hasn't seen, not meaning they can work out.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: Two wrong answers are arguable. 'Hidden' echoes the treasure hidden in a field (Matt 13:44), and treasures kept in a storeroom could reasonably be called hidden. 'Buried' is just as arguable. A baker could defend either one.

rule.text: If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
